title: Special Collector's Disc
lead: A broad starter library for the magazine's first issue.
highlights: More than 200 PC retro games advertised on the sleeve.
75 emulators covering a range of older systems.
context: The available issue 1 PDF lists a coverdisc guide on p. 92, but the scan ends before that page. These contents are taken from the photographed sleeve, not a checked CD image.

title: Retro Gamer System
lead: A game collection that also gives readers a way to make their own.
highlights: More than 100 retro PC games advertised on the sleeve.
A 30-day demo of Clickteam's Multimedia Fusion 1.5.
context: The magazine's *Sub-Attack* tutorial uses that demo to build a submarine game. It lets readers save project files but cannot export a standalone executable.

title: Gremlin's Greatest Hits
lead: Gremlin's back catalogue, organised by original computer format.
highlights: Games from seven formats, with matching emulators.
Scans of Gremlin adverts and game inlays.
context: The printed guide claims more than 250 games; the sleeve says more than 200. The difference is worth preserving because both counts appeared in the original packaging.

title: Retro Collection
lead: A mixed-media disc that works in both a CD player and a computer.
highlights: 18 retro-themed audio tracks for a standard CD player.
PC remakes, emulators, utilities and video files in the computer session.
context: The guide explains how to use the Windows browser to find programs and how the audio tracks play separately from the data files.

title: Retro Gaming Extravaganza
lead: Original C64 material sits alongside contemporary PC remakes.
highlights: More than 50 PC retro games and 20 emulators.
18 Commodore 64 games and demos, plus four C64 music videos.
GameBase 64 for browsing and launching C64 software.
context: The mix of original files, remakes and tools shows how the magazine expected readers to move between historical software and the active emulation scene.

title: Beneath a Steel Sky
lead: The complete Revolution Software adventure is the headline game.
highlights: Full *Beneath a Steel Sky* game data for PC and Mac.
20 further full games and playable demos.
ScummVM supplied as the compatibility layer.
context: The guide walks readers through locating the adventure's files and adding them in ScummVM, recording the setup the editors recommended at the time.

title: Retro 50
lead: Fifty recent PC games sample the retro-inspired development scene.
highlights: Arcade, adventure and puzzle games.
More than an hour of video completing 160 ZX Spectrum games.
Demos from Superior Software and Trymedia.
context: The Spectrum footage ties into the issue's *Over the Rainbow* feature, giving readers a visual companion to the printed article.

title: Graftgold Collection
lead: A publisher archive paired with rare footage of a cancelled system.
highlights: 50 Graftgold games across six formats, including *Paradroid*, *Uridium* and *Quazatron*.
Bundled emulators and platform-specific launch instructions.
More than 40 minutes of Konix Multi System footage.
context: The guide lists the original platforms, while the video gives this CD value beyond the games themselves.

title: Retro Remakes Collection
lead: Two 2004 competitions capture the breadth of hobbyist game making.
highlights: All 76 Retro Remakes Competition entries.
Every entry in the 2004 Interactive Fiction Competition.
context: Graphical remakes and text adventures share the disc. The guide explains how to search for a title and extract entries supplied as archives.

title: The Games Factory
lead: Play the remakes, then use the included tools to build a game.
highlights: 50 PC retro games and remakes.
The complete Home Version of Clickteam's The Games Factory.
A PDF manual and a printed bat-and-ball tutorial.
context: The tutorial introduces the Storyboard, Level and Event editors. The magazine says this Home Version is neither time-limited nor feature-restricted.

title: Durell Big 40 Hits
lead: Durell's games are presented with both emulators and recorded play.
highlights: More than 40 games across seven formats, including *Saboteur*, *Turbo Esprit* and *Thanatos*.
Emulators for running the original versions on PC or Mac.
Spectrum playthrough videos for *Critical Mass*, *Saboteur*, *Thanatos* and *Turbo Esprit*.
context: The recordings make the disc useful even when a reader does not set up every original platform.

title: Llamarama
lead: Jeff Minter's 8-bit catalogue accompanies the issue's feature on its creator.
highlights: 65 Llamasoft games across seven formats.
Titles include *Hover Bovver*, *Gridrunner* and *Revenge of the Mutant Camels*.
Bundled emulators including Spectaculator and blueMSX.
context: The printed walkthrough helps readers run the original files, turning the CD into a cross-platform view of Minter's early work.

title: Amiga Forever 6.0
lead: A complete Amiga emulation package anchors this issue's disc.
highlights: WinUAE and WinFellow emulators with Amiga ROM files.
Amiga games, demos and utilities.
More than 50 PC retro remakes alongside the main package.
context: The guide covers installation, making the disc an entry point into Amiga software as well as a larger remake collection.

title: The Ur-Quan Masters
lead: The complete *Star Control II* port leads a space-themed disc.
highlights: The full PC and Mac version of *The Ur-Quan Masters* with speech and music.
Additional PC retro games in the usual disc browser.
context: The printed guide offers installation steps and an introduction to exploration and combat, so readers can begin with the featured game rather than browsing the CD unguided.

title: 105 Essential Emulators
lead: A tool-focused issue covering a wide range of old hardware.
highlights: 105 emulators advertised on the sleeve.
PC programs spanning machines from the ZX80 and Oric Atmos to later consoles.
context: The guide distinguishes installers from compressed archives and explains how to search, extract and run programs. This disc documents the emulation ecosystem rather than one game catalogue.

title: The Elder Scrolls Arena
lead: Bethesda's complete first *Elder Scrolls* game comes with a practical DOS setup guide.
highlights: The full version of *The Elder Scrolls: Arena*.
DOSBox and the ordinary Retro Gamer disc browser.
context: The magazine walks through installing the game, mounting a drive in DOSBox and launching it from the emulator.

title: Ultimate 2D Shoot-'Em-Up Collection
lead: Fifty homebrew shooters show how developers reworked arcade conventions.
highlights: Vertical and horizontal PC shooters.
Featured games include *Thunder Slash*, *Cloudphobia*, *G-Type* and *Noiz2sa*.
context: The magazine gives individual games space in its guide, making this a snapshot of contemporary independent development rather than a collection of original commercial ROMs.

title: The Last Ninja Trilogy
lead: The final monthly CD focuses on the original *Last Ninja* games.
highlights: Original 8-bit ROMs for all three games, supplied through Play It.
Emulators including WinVICE for C64 and ZX32 for ZX Spectrum.
A printed walkthrough of the first two stages of the original game.
context: The next issue announced that the monthly coverdisc had ended, making this collection the close of the magazine's CD run.
